I will keep both crops, but I will put more land into spring maize and less into cotton. I have only 7 mu and a 2-person household, and some labor goes off-farm, so I will lean toward the crop that is simpler and faster for me to manage. Maize fits that better, especially with well irrigation. I will still keep some cotton because I have long experience with it and I do not want to give it up completely. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, do rotary tillage, apply a moderate-to-high fertilizer rate, irrigate a few times if rainfall is short, and keep pesticide use limited unless pressure rises. For cotton, I will use improved seed, keep fertilizer balanced but not excessive, irrigate a few times through key growth stages, and plan for more pesticide sprays than maize because cotton usually needs closer insect control. I am aiming for stable yield more than maximum yield, because with my age, labor situation, and small area, I value a plan I can finish on time and manage well.
